skills.name: smarteverything-appliances
skills.description: Runs and reads appliances with programs or jobs: the washer-dryer, microwave, network printers, TVs (power, inputs, apps, Wake-on-LAN), robot vacuums (start, rooms, zones, docking), air purifiers, humidifiers, contact, leak and smoke sensors and the AIBI desk robot. Use for “start the washer on cotton”, “print this PDF”, “switch the TV to HDMI 2” or “vacuum the kitchen”. Not for lights and plugs (smarteverything-home) or the treadmill, toothbrush and bottle (smarteverything-wellness-devices).
skills.content:
# Appliances

Read `device_read` first: appliances refuse commands for reasons the state shows (remote control off, door open, child lock, a running cycle), and the refusal names the reason, which you report as given. `device_control` sets one capability per call: send the settings first, check each result, and send a start only after they succeeded.

## Washer-dryer

Read `device_read` first. The machine's remote control must be on (`remote_control` true) or Start fails; report that reason. Send power (if off), the program and then each option it uses, one `device_control` call each, and check every result succeeded; only then send `cycle_start`. Changing the program resets its options, so send every option you want. For finish-by set `delay_mode` Finish Wash and `delay_minutes`. Options are locked during a cycle. Use `door_release` only when paused with the door line saying it is safe. Never start Drum Clean with laundry inside. `cycle_stop` needs your confirmation unless the person said stop. Report `remaining_minutes` and the finish time from it.

## Microwave

Read `device_read` first. Every cooking write needs Remote control on, the door closed and the child lock off; a refusal names which, so report it. Set the Cooking mode in its own `device_control` call, then in the next send the Set cooking duration (an object with `operationTime` as hours:minutes:seconds), Microwave power and Cooking temperature that mode accepts (the capability lists the allowed values; an option the mode lacks is refused with the reason), and only then Start cooking. Some modes can be set but only started on the appliance: say Press Start on the microwave. Pause cooking and Stop cooking need only remote control. Read the Operating state, progress and finish time from `device_read`, and past cooking cycles from the `readDeviceLog` operation.

## Printers

A network printer (IPP, AirPrint-compatible) is a device of family `printer` (`device_find` with that family). `device_read` gives its state (`printer_state`: idle, printing, stopped), the queue (`queue`: running or paused), the number of waiting jobs, the problem keyword if it has one, the pages printed today, the lowest supply and the days left, and each supply, tray and output bin as readings. Supplies are cartridges, toner and a waste tank; a level the printer does not report is unknown, never zero. The waste tank is a supply that fills up: it is low when it is nearly full.

- Printing, the queue, history and statistics use the printer plugin's `printer` (read) and `printer_action` tools; find them with `tool_search`. Read views: overview, supplies, trays, queue, jobs, stats, options (what this printer can do and the print settings it accepts), candidates, settings (owner only). Omit `printer` when only one is set up.
- `printer_action` takes an `action`: print (a PDF, JPEG, PNG or WebP from an upload, an attachment or a computer file; ask for copies, sides, colour, quality or paper only when the person said so, and read the options view first so you never send a setting the printer does not list), test_page, cancel, hold and release (a job key), pause and resume the queue, identify (beep or flash so the person can find it), the printer's own web page link, and configure for the caller's own print defaults. Adding a printer, rescanning, forgetting it, cancelling every job, trusting a new certificate, entering its sign-in and clearing its history are owner only; an encrypted printer with a self-signed certificate asks the owner to confirm its fingerprint first. Never ask for or repeat a printer password in chat.
- A member sees and cancels only their own jobs; other people's document names are hidden and the owner sees everyone's. Print only what the person asked for and say what you sent (name, copies, sides). A paused or stopped printer, an empty tray or a jam is reported as given with the plain cause from the problem keyword; do not retry a refused print.
- Ink and toner: `history_read` reads `printer` supply levels over time, the supplies view gives burn rate, days left and a forecast of when it runs out, and a cartridge replacement is a mark on that history. Say when a forecast is rough because there is little history.
- The printer sends plugin events (`job_started`, `job_finished` with the result, `problem_added` and `problem_cleared`, `supply_low`, `supply_empty`, `supply_replaced`, `restarted`, `offline_long`); see `smarteverything-automations`.

## TVs

Read `device_read` first; its `television` part gives the direct link (`direct_link`: the screen's `address` and the `mac` that wakes it, or null when not linked) and the names given to inputs (`inputNames`, input id to name; the TV's own input ids come from the `input_source` options). A linked screen is controlled over the home network first (power, keys including numbers and colours, apps) with SmartThings only as the backup, and it is turned on with Wake-on-LAN to the MAC the link read from the screen itself. A sleeping TV reads off, not broken; `power` on works only when the device has a wake path (the direct link, remote power on while SmartThings sees it, Wake-on-LAN when `wakeAddress` is set, or an IR remote), otherwise say how to fix it. To link a screen, the person opens that screen's settings in the app while it is on, chooses Link directly, picks the screen and chooses Allow on the screen with its remote; the AI cannot approve that prompt. The `listTelevisionCandidates` operation (`operation_call`; `tool_read` gives its input) lists the Samsung screens on the network with their address, MAC and the device each is already linked to. The `findTelevision` operation looks once for a screen that is not linked directly, saves its address when it is certain which screen it is and starts the link so the screen shows its Allow prompt; it does nothing for a linked screen, and the person still chooses Allow on the screen. An offline screen with a `wakeAddress` and no direct link is woken over the home network and the command succeeds only once it comes online; when it does not, tell the person to turn on Power On with Mobile on the screen (`last_wake_worked_at` says when a wake last worked). Without a direct link or a `wakeAddress`, suggest linking it directly; only if the person prefers, set the screen's network MAC address (on the TV: Settings, General, Network, Network Status, IP Settings, or About) with `device_edit` (`wakeAddress`, null clears it); never guess it from another screen. Open an app with one `app_launch`, not key sequences. Navigate with `remote_key` names such as `up`, `ok`, `back`, `home`, `vol_up`, `mute`, `n0` to `n9`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`; a key the TV's paths cannot send fails with a reason, so report it. Picture and sound modes are the options `device_read` lists. IR presses are unconfirmed.

Use `widget_show` for a live device, remote or weather card. A widget a plugin adds is a board type like any other (`pluginId.widgetId`, listed by `plugin_read`): `widget_show` kind `board` shows it and the board layout operations place it on the Home board.

## Robot vacuum

A robot vacuum is a device of family `vacuum` (`device_find` with that family). `device_read` gives its `vacuum` part: `phase` (the operating state, such as charging, cleaning or returning), `status` in the words the app shows, `battery_percent`, the current `job` (scope, mode, room names, progress, time), `rooms` (id, name, area in m2), saved `zones` (no-go, no-mop and walls, in metres), the `station` (dust, mop wash, drying, tanks), `consumables` (life and time left), the `map` (version, age, dock and robot position), the `last_clean` and `camera`. A `problems` list says what could not be read; report it, never guess the missing value.

- Start, stop and dock are the `cleaning` capability: `device_control` with the value `start`, `pause`, `resume`, `dock` or `stop`; a whole-home clean is `start`. Rooms by name are the `raw:clean_rooms` action: value `{ "rooms": ["Kitchen", "Hall"] }` with optional `repeats` (1 to 3), `suction` (silent, standard, strong, turbo), `water` (off, level_1 to level_3) and `mode` (sweep, sweep_mop, sweep_then_mop). Use the room names from the `rooms` list, never ids you made up; an unknown name is refused and the refusal lists the rooms. Zones are the `raw:clean_zones` action: `{ "zones": [{ "x1", "y1", "x2", "y2" }] }` in metres on the robot's map, at most 5, taken from the map read, never guessed.
- Suction, mop level and every setting (carpet, mop wash, drying, dust collection, do not disturb, volume) are capabilities set one per call with their role's label and allowed values from `device_read`. Changing the mop wash or dust settings changes what the station does on the next clean.
- The map: `device_read` already gives each room's id, name, area and bounds in metres (`min` and `max` corners, y up), the zones, the dock and the robot position; read zone coordinates from there before a zone clean or an area edit. `getVacuumScene` (`operation_call`; `tool_read` gives its input) gives the same compact map for a `slot` (current, saved or backup), so use it for the saved or backup map; the outlines, walls and trail stay in the app. `listVacuumCleans` lists past cleans with the rooms, area, time and how each ended. `editVacuumAreas` replaces no-go areas, no-mop areas and walls (at most 10 in total) and returns the previous ones so a change can be undone. `setVacuumRoomSettings` sets a room's floor or hides it; a map room has no name of its own to set, it shows the name of the home room it is linked to.
- Room links: each room on the robot's map can be linked to a room of the home; `device_read` shows the linked `home_room` per map room and `unlinked_rooms` in the map. `listVacuumRoomLinks` lists the map rooms with their link, a name suggestion for unlinked ones, stale links whose map room is gone and every home room with the map room using it. Link only when the person asks or confirms: `setVacuumRoomLink` with the map room id and the home room id (a suggestion is never a link by itself); a home room links to one map room per robot, so a home room already used is refused unless `move` is true, which leaves the other map room unlinked. `removeVacuumRoomLink` unlinks a map room or removes a stale link.
- Why a command is not accepted: the refusal names the reason and you report it as given. Common ones are a command sent while the robot is in a phase that cannot take it (a sleeping or updating robot, a fault, mapping), no map yet, a room name that is not on the map, or a dock that is busy washing or drying. A command the robot accepted only means it was sent; the state change confirms it, so read `device_read` again before saying it started. Do not repeat a start whose outcome is unknown.
- Faults come as an active fault with the robot's description; report it as given and do not retry the clean until the person has dealt with it.
- Cleaning schedules are SmartEverything automations (a time trigger that starts the clean), never a schedule stored on the robot; create them with the automation tools (see `smarteverything-automations`). The do-not-disturb period is a separate setting and never starts a clean.
- Consumables show life and time left; call a reset only when the person says the part was replaced. Never reset, delete a map, change Wi-Fi or update firmware for the person unless they ask in those words.
- Camera privacy: a vacuum with a camera shows `camera` in its part. Never switch the camera video on, set or ask for its video password, or describe what it sees; the person does that in the app. Say that the video switch is the person's choice.

## Air, sensors and the desk robot

- Air purifier: Purifier mode (role `purifier_mode`), Favourite level and fan mode are the controls; humidifier: `target_humidity`, `mode` and `mist_level`. Child lock is a setting. Filter life and days left are readings; call `filter_reset` only when the person says the filter was replaced.
- Contact, motion, leak and smoke sensors only report: read them with `device_read`, find when they changed with `history_read` or `event_find` (opened, leak, smoke), and react to them with an automation, never with a command.
- AIBI, the small desk robot, is a device with one control, Move or act: send an object with `action` and `options` through `device_control`. It moves only while AIBI is in a conversation (the move rides with its next answer) and is refused with that reason otherwise, so `voice_speak` to it or ask the person to talk to it first. Its plugin tools (`plugin_read`, `tool_search`) read its status, what it heard and did, and the moves it offers with their options (read them before choosing a move), and can make it forget its conversations, which only the person's request justifies.

skills.name: smarteverything-automation-nodes
skills.description: The automation node language: nodes and wires, ports and typed values, logic, maths, text and list nodes, device, camera, TV, computer, lock, chat and plugin nodes, run mode, the If it fails exit, Custom Nodes, loops, variables and persistence. Use it while writing or patching a program, or when automation_edit check reports a node or port problem. Not for choosing a scene, schedule or automation (smarteverything-automations) or for triggers (smarteverything-automation-triggers).
skills.content:
# Automation nodes

The node catalog is the contract: `automation_read` view catalog lists every kind with its ports, types, picker sources, run modes and plugin origin, and only those kinds and port names exist. Every port holds a literal or a wire; there are no formulas, so every calculation is its own node.

## Nodes and wires only

An automation is a flow chart of nodes joined by wires. Formulas, expressions and text templates do not exist anywhere: a port that needs a worked out value gets a wire from the output of a node that works it out. Build every program this way, step by step:

1. Every port, branch condition, case condition, structured output, variable start value and `admit` holds exactly one of two things: a constant `{"lit": value}` or a wire `{"wire": {"from": "<source>", "port": "<output>"}}`. Nothing else is accepted.
2. A wire's `from` is the `key` of a node that comes earlier (a loop or try gives `item`, `index` or `error` to the steps inside it), or one of five sources: `trigger` (the outputs of the trigger that fired, plus `key` and `at`), `inputs` (the inputs of a Custom Node or called automation), `vars` (a variable, by name), `home` (`timeZone`, `name`, `latitude`, `longitude`) and `run` (`id`, `startedAt`). `port` is one output name. To read a field inside a record, wire the record into Get field (`object.get`) and wire on from its `value`.
3. Work values out with calculation nodes. They never act, and can sit anywhere before the node that reads them: Compare (`logic.compare`: equal, not equal, greater, at least, less, at most), `logic.between`, Is one of (`logic.in`), And and Or (`logic.and`, `logic.or`: two to four flags wired into `a`, `b`, `c`, `d`), Not, Has a value (`logic.exists`), First available (`logic.coalesce`, with a `default`), Choose (`logic.select`: `condition`, then `whenTrue`, else `whenFalse`), Which trigger (`logic.trigger_is`), Add, Subtract, Multiply (two to four values in `a` to `d`), Divide, Remainder, Round, Clamp, Message (`text.format`: a fixed `template` whose `{a}` to `{d}` are filled from the values wired into `a` to `d`), Text check (`text.test`: contains, starts with, ends with, equals, is empty), Join, Count items (`list.length`), Get item (`list.get`: first, last or by index), Any item, Every item, Keep where and Find (`list.any`, `list.all`, `list.filter`, `list.find`: each compares every item, or one `field` of every record, by `test` with `value`), Field of each (`list.field`), Get field, Convert (`util.convert`: to number, text, on/off, duration, moment or list) and Lookup table (`util.lookup`).
4. Decide with wires too: an If branch `when`, a switch case `{"when": ...}`, the wait-for-condition `condition`, `admit` and the `condition` of `trigger.becomes_true` each take a wire to a flag, usually the `result` of a Compare, And, Or, Not or Has a value node. A switch on a value takes the wire in `subject` and fixed cases (`eq`, `in`, `range`).
5. An optional output (optional in the catalog) cannot feed a port that needs a value: test it with Has a value and branch, or pass it through First available with a `default`. A number wire fits any number port; for another type wire it through Convert.
6. Effects (device commands, notifications, tool calls, Value and variable changes) are always their own nodes on the run path, never inside a calculation.

Example: lights to step 1 when the step is 0 or no light is on. “stepIsZero” is a Compare with `a` a wire from `vars` port `step`, `op` eq and `b` 0; “noneOn” is a Compare with `a` a wire from “onNow” port `count` and `b` 0; `either` is an Or with `a` wired from “stepIsZero” port `result` and `b` from “noneOn” port `result`; the `flow.if` branch `when` is a wire from `either` port `result`.

Per-room logic is one Custom Node, never copies. Give it inputs for what differs per room (for example `lights` a target, `event` a choice, `sensors` a list of devices, `allowed` a flag), keep what it must remember in `persist` variables, and build its body from the nodes above. Each room's automation then holds its triggers and one `fn.call` with the room's constants and wires, for example `event` wired from a Lookup table or Choose fed by a wire from `trigger` port `key`. Change the Custom Node once and every room follows.

## Nodes

Common nodes: `device.set` (`target` device, devices, room or group; `control`; `to`; `percent`; `by` adds to a number; `transition` fades where the device can), the temporary-set node of the `device` group (the control returns to its base after a time, when its `while` condition turns false, or when stopped; `priority` orders overlapping changes), `device.get`, `scene.run`, `flow.if`, `flow.switch`, `flow.repeat`, `flow.while`, the for-each loop, `flow.wait`, the wait-for-event and wait-for-condition nodes of the `flow` group, `notify.person` (really pushes), `notify.feed`, `notify.speak`, `var.get`, `var.set` and `var.change` (Values and variables), `automation.run`, `automation.stop` and `fn.call` (a Custom Node). A run keeps going when a scene or automation it uses is edited. Loops have no limit unless one is set: `flow.repeat`, `flow.while`, `flow.do_until` and the loop-until-break node `flow.forever` take an optional `limit` (`iterations`, `time` in ms, `onLimit` fail or end, optional `note`), the for-each loop runs any number of items at once with `concurrency`, and the automation's `budgets` (steps in a row, steps per run, loop passes, run chain length, side-by-side branches) are optional too; only `commandsPerMinute` (600) and the run state size guard (`runStateBytes`, 8 MiB) have defaults. A run never blocks the hub and `automation_stop` ends it at any time. A `flow.forever` needs a Break, Return or Stop inside or a `limit`; the checker names what a loop lacks.

`computer.audio` takes an `action` (`volume`, `mute`, `default`, `app_volume`, `app_mute`, `app_output`) with typed ports: `kind` (output or input), `device`, `app`, `level` and `muted`. `computer.display` takes an `action` (`enable`, `disable`, `mode`, `scale`, `rotation`, `primary`, `position`, `mirror`, `brightness`, `hdr`, `vrr`, `night_light`, `keep`, `revert`) with typed ports: `output` (the screen), `width`, `height`, `refreshHz`, `scale`, `rotation`, `relativeTo` and `side`, `mirrorOf`, `brightness`, `enabled`, `vrr`, `nightLight` and `temperature`. Display settings are always `computer.display`, never `tool.call`. Read `computer_read` first for the exact names and the features the computer offers; a node the computer does not offer, a device that is not a computer, or (for a member) someone else's computer is refused when saved. Nobody is asked while it runs, so a screen change that can blank a screen (`mode`, `scale`, `position`, rotation, main screen, turning a screen off, mirroring) goes back by itself after 15 seconds unless someone keeps it at the computer. Add `keep: true` to keep it automatically once the hub has read the screen back and seen the change applied; if it does not match, the change is reverted at once and the node fails.

The run policy `mode` is single (default), restart, queue or parallel; queue needs `max` (and may take `maxWait`), parallel may take one. `key` names runs so `automation_stop` can end only those. Custom Nodes (`fn.call`) may call themselves or each other: recursion is allowed with no depth limit, and a runaway recursion is stopped by `automation_stop` or fails when its run state grows past `runStateBytes`. An `automation.run` node refuses to start an automation already in its own chain of runs unless it sets `allowSelf`.

`ai.wake` (`person`, optional `chat`, `instruction`) wakes that person's AI with what happened. `tool.call` (`person`, `tool`, `args`) calls an enabled assistant tool without an AI turn, using the exact arguments from `tool_read`. Use it only for a tool no node covers: lights, climate, appliances, cameras, vacuums, TVs, calls, computers, phones, locks, speech, pictures, chats and health all have nodes (next section), and a plugin's own actions are plugin nodes. Both are for the owner.

Every automation records who made it in `author` (`via` person or assistant, and `profile_id`), and a plugin in `origin`; `author` is null only for automations made before this was recorded. Never create, change, switch, run or remove an automation the person did not ask for, and never touch one only because it looks wrong: say what you noticed.

## First-class nodes

Look in the catalog group before anything else: each of these is a node with typed ports and pickers, and `tool.call` never replaces one. A target port takes devices, a room or a group, and all of them are sent to at once.

- Lights: `light.set` (`power`, `brightness` in percent, `color`, `colorTemperature` in kelvin, `effect`, `transition`) sends each light one command with everything in it. A colour is a name, hex such as `#ff8800`, `{"r":255,"g":0,"b":0}` or `{"hue":0,"saturation":100,"value":100}`; a colour and a colour temperature cannot be combined.
- Climate and appliances: `climate.set` (`power`, `mode`, `temperature` with `unit` c or f, `fan`, `fanSpeed`, `swing`, `oscillation`, `offTimer`), `appliance.set` (a writable `setting`, then `value` typed by it) and `device.action` (press an action button). `ir.appliance_set` brings an infrared appliance to a state (`power`, `mode`, `temperature`, `fan`). `laundry.start`, `laundry.control` and `laundry.read` run and read a washer or dryer.
- Security: `lock.set` (owner only), `alarm.set` (a mode the panel offers) and `cover.set` (open, close, stop or a position).
- Cameras: `camera.snapshot` (the picture id), `camera.record` (clip length in seconds), `camera.move` (a saved `preset` or a `direction` with `steps`) and `camera.set` (privacy, motion, `nightVision`, status light, or every camera). Speech on a camera, speaker, computer or phone, or on a Talk channel, is `notify.speak` (`target`, `channel`, `text`, `priority`, `volume`, `voice`), never `tool.call` with `voice_speak`.
- Vacuums: `vacuum.command` (start, pause, resume, stop, dock, spot), `vacuum.station` (dust, mop and tank jobs), `vacuum.clean_rooms` (home `rooms` matched through the room links; unlinked rooms are left out and listed in `unlinkedRooms`, never guessed) and `vacuum.read`.
- TVs: `tv.control` takes an `action` (power, volume, `input`, `channel`, `app`, remote `key`, art mode, `playback`, picture and sound mode).
- Calls: `call.person` (ring one person's `device`: phone, computer app or any; outputs `answered`, `outcome`, `timedOut`, `outreachId`), `call.open` (talk through a camera or a Talk channel) and `call.end`.
- Computers: `computer.audio` and `computer.display` (above), `computer.power` (lock, sleep, hibernate, restart, shut down, sign out, wake), `computer.system` (power mode, do not disturb, keyboard layout, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, startup apps, services), `computer.app` (open, close, focus, minimise) and `computer.open` (a link or a path). Clicking and typing on a screen stays with the assistant only.
- Phones: `phone.ring`, `phone.sound`, `phone.media`, `phone.open`, `phone.flashlight`, `phone.screen` and `phone.toggle`; `phone.action` is the general one. `notify.person` also takes `image` (a picture id), `priority`, `tag`, `link` and `sound`.
- Pictures and chats: `ai.image` makes a picture and returns a picture id that works wherever a `camera.snapshot` id does (push message, Discord, print); `ai.vision` looks at a picture, a `camera`, or with `source` a computer screen, a computer window or a phone screen. `chat.post` puts a message in a person's chat, `transcript.read` reads what a source heard and `listening.set` changes how a source listens.
- Health and events: `health.today`, `health.range`, `health.read`, the water-logging node of the `health` group and `event.count`. `device.query` finds devices by room, group, family or role.

## Run mode and the If it fails exit

In the catalog `modes` gives a step's default and allowed run mode, and `fallible: true` means it has the If it fails exit. Set a mode, a `timeout` or `onError` in the node's `policy`, or with a patch `set` op (`mode`, `timeout`, each cleared with null).

- `fire_and_forget` (plain commands default to it) continues as soon as the command is handed over; `wait_for_result` (reads, questions and everything else, always) continues when the device confirms or the answer arrives, and fails with `Timeout` when `timeout` passes. Only kinds whose `modes.allowed` lists both accept a mode. A failed send fails the node in either mode; a missing confirmation after a send never fails or reroutes the run.
- Outputs the catalog marks `waitOnly` (for example `ok` and `spokenOn` of `notify.speak`) exist only when the node waits. Wiring one from a node that sends is an error in `automation_edit` check: set that node to `wait_for_result`.
- Wire a step's `onError` exit (connect from the port `onError`, which also sets `policy.onError` to `route`) to the steps that handle a failure. There, wire from the failing node's `key` the ports `reason` (`Refused`, `Unreachable`, `Timeout`, `Invalid`, `NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Failed`, `LimitExceeded`, `TypeError`, `MathError` or `Unknown`), `message` and optional `code`. An exit nobody wired behaves as `policy.onError` says (`fail`, the default, or `continue`); `BudgetExceeded` and `Cancelled` are never caught. Only fallible kinds have the exit; `flow.try` still does `finally`.

## Typed values

Fill a port with the type the catalog shows: a `choice` takes one of its option ids, a number takes a number inside its `min` and `max` (percent ports 0 to 100), a duration is milliseconds, a `ref` takes an id or a wire. A catalog `pickers` entry names where a port's value comes from (`device.writable_controls`, `climate.modes`, `vacuum.rooms`, `tv.inputs`, `talk.channels`, `voices`, `phone.apps`, `computer.displays`, a plugin's own entities): read the real options with the tool for that area (`device_read`, `computer_read`, `plugin_read`), never invent an id or paste JSON into a text port. A port typed by another (`to` by `control`, `value` by `setting`) takes what that control accepts, in its own unit. Free text is only for text that is itself the content, such as a message or a prompt.

## Plugin nodes

A plugin declares its own nodes, triggers, Values and entity lists, and they are first class. They sit in the catalog group `plugins` with `origin` (kind, id, name) and `available`; an unavailable one carries the reason (plugin switched off, runs as an external local process, owner only). Ids are `plugin.<owner>.<id>` and `trigger.plugin.<owner>.<id>`, where the owner is the plugin id with `-` as `_`, or `driver_<id>` for a local driver. Never use `tool.call` for something a plugin node does; if the node is unavailable, tell the person why instead of falling back to a tool.

## Integration nodes

Read the node catalog (`automation_read` view `catalog`) for exact ports. `ai.ask` runs one model call for a person and returns `text`, `result` (when a `shape` is given), `tokens` and `cost`; it has no tools unless `tools` names them, so give it tools only when none of its inputs come from outside the home. `ai.vision` does the same on pictures or a `camera` (the Bedroom camera stays blocked) and `ai.decide` returns a yes or no `answer` with a `reason`. A member's AI call runs as that member and stops at their budget. `camera.snapshot` stores a picture and returns its id for later `ai.vision` calls. `health.read` and `signal.emit` read the person's health data and act on the signal bus; `http.respond` answers the webhook that started the run, once.

## More nodes

All of these are in the catalog; read it for exact ports. Pure ones only compute and never send anything.

- Devices: `device.snapshot` (Remember state) reads chosen controls of the target at the moment the run reaches it, so a `device.restore` wired straight to it puts back what was there then, however many changes come between; `device.restore` skips offline devices and says which. `device.aggregate` (Across devices) leaves offline devices out of any, all, none, count and the number functions and lists them in its `offline` output. `scene.capture` saves the current values of devices as a scene (`overwrite` must be on to replace one of the same name). `device.fade` moves a number control (brightness by default) from one level to another over a time, paced by the command budget; stopping leaves it at the current level. `device.ensure` sends a value, waits for the device to report it and sends again if it does not, for devices whose cloud drops commands. `device.ir_send` presses a button of a learned infrared remote through its blaster.
- Readings: `computer.read` and `phone.read` return what a computer or phone reports now (a figure it does not report is left out), `signal.latest` reads the newest signal of one kind since the hub started (it never wakes a wait: use the wait-for-event node for that), `weather.forecast` reads the next hours (rain chance, wet hours, lowest and highest temperature, strongest wind) and `date.sun_times` gives sunrise, sunset, twilight, solar noon and golden hour (absent when the sun does not reach that day; fails when no home location is set).
- Flow: `flow.forever` repeats until a Break, Return or Stop. `debug.breakpoint` (Pause here) pauses a dry run or simulation until the person continues.
- Logic: `logic.and`, `logic.or` and `logic.not` combine flags, `logic.changed` tells whether a value differs from the last run of this node in this automation (the first run counts as changed), `logic.count_true` counts true flags against `atLeast` and `atMost`, `logic.xor` is true when exactly one flag is, `logic.day_type` tells weekday, weekend or one of the dates you list (no holiday calendar is built in), `logic.in_schedule` tells whether a moment falls in weekly slots (a slot that ends after midnight belongs to the day it starts on).
- Numbers and chance: `math.convert_unit` converts within one kind of unit (temperature, length, power, energy, pressure, speed, colour temperature, volume), `math.percent` gives a percent of, a percent change or a percent value (a zero base fails), `random.chance` is true with a probability from 0 to 1 and `random.duration` picks a duration between a minimum and a maximum; random results are captured for the run and a simulation can seed them.
- Text: `text.case` trims, changes case or makes a slug, `text.slice` cuts, shortens with an ellipsis and pads, `text.speakable` writes a number, duration or moment the way it is said aloud (numbers and durations are English).
- Lists: `list.range` (numbers from one to another in steps), `list.slice` (a run, the first N or the last N), `list.sort` (numbers or texts, or records by a `field`; mixed kinds fail), `list.unique` (optionally by a `field`), `list.combine` (join, union, intersection or difference) and `list.reshape` (reverse, flatten one level, chunk or zip). To work through a list item by item use the for-each loop with `collect`, or `var.change` inside it to add up.
- Records: `object.fields` takes a record apart into keys, values and entries or builds one from entries, `object.merge` (a later record wins; `deep` merges inside records), `object.pick` keeps or omits listed fields and `object.remove` drops the field at a path (a missing path fails unless ignored).
- Time: `date.next` is the next moment a time of day comes round on chosen weekdays (daylight saving handled) and the start-of node of the `date` group is the first moment or last millisecond of a day, week (Monday), month or year in the home time zone.
- Secrets: `var.secret` hands a stored secret to a node that accepts one, such as the `auth` of `http.request`; its value is never shown, recorded or readable as text. Owner only.

skills.name: smarteverything-automation-triggers
skills.description: Reference for what starts an automation: device values and events, computer app events, camera detections, wake words, calls, people arriving and leaving, appliance, safety and vacuum events, phone events, plugin and health events, times, sun times, holds and windows. Use while building or fixing a trigger, for “when someone arrives home”, “if the baby cries” or “after sunset”. Not for the program itself (smarteverything-automations) or the node list (smarteverything-automation-nodes).
skills.content:
# Automation triggers

Discover the trigger before writing it: `signal_read` view catalogue with a query gives each trigger with its source, kind, field, match keys and how to use it. Anything not found there does not exist and never fires.

## Build from real contracts

Discover before writing: `automation_read` view `catalog` (filter `query`, `group` or `kind`) lists node kinds with their ports, types and examples, plus Custom Nodes; use only kinds and port names it shows, and read `device_read` for every device control a node uses. For a trigger, `signal_read` with view `catalogue` and a `query` (a device, a room, a plugin or what you want to react to, optionally a `group`) gives each row's source and kind, the ways to use it (`how`), its field and match keys and a plain sentence; view `kinds` lists every signal kind with its match values and view `values` gives current examples. Never invent a signal kind, a match key or a trigger from a device name. A computer is a device: its readings (battery level, processor and graphics load and temperature, memory and disk use, network rates, locked, front app, display count on) and controls (volume, mute, audio output, microphone mute, brightness, night light, Do Not Disturb, power mode, playback, power actions) are capability keys in `device_read`. Per-app sound and per-screen changes have no key: they are the `computer.audio` and `computer.display` nodes.

A comparison against a missing value or a value of another kind fails the run: the home data is missing, so say so.

A match key with `values: null` has no fixed list and takes exact observed `data` or `details` values. Empty latest values do not prove a trigger unsupported. For camera sound events keep the discovered detection (Baby crying, Unusual sound, Loud sound are distinct; plain Sound is broad).

Computer app events: the events `app_opened` (an app gets its first window), `app_closed` (its last window goes), `app_focused` (it comes to the front) and `app_unfocused` (it leaves the front) carry the match keys `app` (name), `appId`, `title`, `user` and `personId`, and `event_find` reads them. To wait for an app to stay open or in front, trigger on the `computer` signals `app_open` or `app_focus` (value true or false, `field` the app id, `subject` the computer, match `app`) with test `{is: eq, to: true}` and `hold`, for example Firefox open for 30 minutes is `hold` 1800; each app is tracked on its own. They need the computer's `app_events` permission together with `apps` (on by default, owner only, in `computer_read` `permissions`) and are reported only by Linux computers with KDE or X11 window control.

Provider events with no named kind: nothing a device reports as an event is dropped. An unnamed Xiaomi event, a SmartThings attribute not shown as a device value, a camera event type that is not a known detection and a read-only Tuya alert data point (alarm, alert, warning, fault, tamper, siren, trigger) that turned active all arrive as `activity` events. They carry a plain `summary`, and their own facts: `event` and `miotEvent` (Xiaomi name) with `arguments` (its values, not matchable), `attribute`, `capability`, `topic` and `component` (SmartThings), `code` and `value` (Tuya), `eventType` and `hasClip` (cameras). Read them with `event_find` and trigger on `source: event`, `kind: activity` with any of these as match keys. Camera detections also carry `source`, `eventType`, `hasClip`, `fileId` and `imgStoreId`; appliance events `family`, `item` and `state`. Plain on/off and number changes are device values: trigger on those with the `device` signals.

Activity feed for any signal: a signal kind marked `feed` in `signal_read` (plugin events by default, hub notices such as `storm`) is also recorded once as a `event_find` row of kind `signal`, with `details` source, kind, field, label, subject, value, `profileId` when it belongs to one person and `data` when it has any. Narrow those rows with `event_find` `source` (the signal source, for example `hub` or `plugin_router`) and `signalKind`; a person's AI sees only their own rows. A plugin author can set `feed: false` on a manifest event to keep it out of the feed; it still triggers automations.

Wake, listening and calls: the `listening` signals `wake_heard` (once per settled wake contest; `subject` the winning camera, phone, computer or channel id, or `discord`; `value` its loudness in dBFS; match `source`, `winner` and `decidedBy` only, capped at 6 a minute with a burst of 3 per source) and `state` (per listening source: `value` is `on`, `off`, `paused:<reason>`, `budget_used_up`, `mic_permission_lost`, `no_host` or `offline`; match `state`, `source` and `reason` privacy, in_call, discord_call or no_openrouter_key; camera transcript pauses are not reported) and the `call` signals `started` and `ended` (`subject` and `profileId` the person; match `source` chat, orb, palette, assist, assistant, shortcut or hosted, plus `person` and `device`; `ended` also `ending` and its `value` is the length in seconds, so test `gt` with 600 for calls over ten minutes) and `outreach` (`value` and match `state`: ringing, answered, declined, missed, failed or sent, plus `how` and `target`; trigger on `ringing` then `missed` for an unanswered AI call). All are recorded as `signal` rows in `event_find`; `started` and `outreach` survive a flood; none carries what was said; the owner can switch the `listening` or `call` source off with `updateTriggerSettings`.

People arriving and leaving: the core `presence` signals `person_arrived` and `person_left` (match `person_id`) fire once when a person's combined home state flips to home, and once when it flips to away (their first linked device or paired phone shows them home, and the last one has been gone past the grace period). `trigger.presence` listens to them; use it, not a plugin's own event. They are capped at 6 a minute per person. As a condition, the router device has `raw:people_home` (how many are home) and one boolean `raw:home_<person id>` per tracked person (person ids come from `who_is_home`), readable with `device_read` and usable in `compare` like any control. Presence never selects the server route.

Flood protection: every signal source has a rate cap per device, field or kind, and a signal repeating faster than its cap is dropped, so never trigger on a continuous reading by itself: use a window (avg, min, max, count), a comparison with `hold`, or a crossing. Excess is logged and the `hub` signal `storm` (match `source`, `kind`, `reason`) reports it; alarms and rings (`urgent` kinds) survive a flood. The owner switches a source or one `source/kind` off, or on for opt-in kinds (`optIn`), with `operation_call` `updateTriggerSettings` (`sources`: name to true or false, `kinds`: `source/kind` to true or false, null restores the default); `settings_read` shows `trigger_settings`, and an off kind drops its signals without a trace, so check it when a trigger never fires.

Commands and service connections: every command sent to a device is a `device` signal `command` (`subject` the device, `field` the control key, value what was sent) with match `status` (`sent`, `done`, `failed`, `timed_out`), `capability`, `cause` (`app`, `assistant`, `automation`, `scene`) and, when it failed, `error`; only `failed` and `timed_out` reach the activity feed (`event_find` kind `signal`), so trigger on `sent` or `done` for the rest. A connection to a service (Xiaomi, Tuya, SmartThings, Samsung TV, local) is the `provider` signal `status` (value and match `state`: `linked`, `attention` when it needs signing in again, `down` when it cannot be reached; also `provider`, `problem`, `error`). Each outage and new adapter failure is one `provider_error` event, never one per device: while a service is in `attention` or `down`, its devices' `device_offline` and `device_online` events are not recorded, so read the `provider` status (the device still shows offline).

Device values, online and lifecycle: every `device` signal `state` also carries the facts of its device as match keys, so one trigger covers a whole group: `family` (light, fan, lock, computer, ...), `kind`, `roomId`, `provider`, `name`, `role` (what the value is, shared across models, such as `power`, `brightness`, `fault`), `unit` and `cause` (`physical` when someone used the device itself, `app`, `assistant`, `automation` or `schedule`, read from the command that preceded the change). Any light turning on in the Study is `match` family light and roomId of that room, `field` `power`, test `{is: eq, to: true}`; only a wall switch flip is `cause` physical. A value turning unknown is a signal with value null (an alarm cleared, playback stopped); the first value a device ever reports is not a signal. Numbers are announced only when they moved by at least the control's step and at most every 2 seconds (every 10 seconds for graphed readings such as latency), and the newest value follows when that pause ends, so use a window or `hold` for slow drift. `device` signal `online` (value true or false, every device including a computer, match the same facts; the activity feed keeps `device_online` and `device_offline` events) gives `hold` of 10 minutes on `eq` false for offline for ten minutes. `device` signal `lifecycle` is a moment with match `change`: `added`, `removed`, `renamed` (data `from`, `to`), `moved` (room), `replaced` (other hardware, `from`, `to` model), `capabilities_changed` (`added`, `removed` control keys) and `firmware_changed`; it reaches the activity feed as `signal` rows. Renames and moves made in the app are not lifecycle signals.

Water bottle events: a LARQ bottle sends `activity` events whose `activity` is drink, refill, uv_clean, goal_reached or drinks_imported (a drink carries `ml` and `levelMl`; imported drinks older than 30 minutes arrive as one drinks_imported event), a `fault` event with the `fault` code and `name`, and `maintenance` events whose `maintenance` is battery_low or filter_due. Its `water_level`, `bottle_volume`, `battery`, `bottle_charging` and `bottle_state` are `device` state signals and conditions (the person's water total for the day is `water` of the `health.today` node, and the bottle level or the goal_reached event also work). Nodes can set `reminder_colour`, `reminder_interval`, `quiet_hours` and the window times (applied when the bottle next wakes) and stop `uv_clean`; an automation can never start one.

Treadmill events: a WalkingPad sends `activity` events whose `phase` is started, paused, resumed, finished or goal_reached (match `walker`, `kind` walk, jog, run or intervals, `goal`; the finished event also carries `distance_m`, `duration_s` and `steps`, read with `event_find`, not matchable), a `fault` event with the `code` (E01 to E13, or safety_stop), a `maintenance` event with `reason` lubrication_due, and a `button` event with `button` up, down, stop or mode. Its belt state, speed, mode and child lock are `device` state signals (use `hold` or a crossing for speed). A `device.set` that starts the belt or raises its speed is refused unless the owner allowed remote start, so keep stop and pause nodes for safety automations and say when a start node will be refused. A Kingsmith G15 also has `belt_incline` as a state signal and condition (whole steps): trigger on it only with a `gte` or `lte` test, `hold` and `rearm` (for example `gte` 8, `rearm` 6, `hold` 20 seconds), never on every change. A `device.set` on `belt_incline` is refused unless the owner allowed remote incline, only raises up to the remote cap and never runs while nobody walks, so do not depend on it. `goal_reached` exists only for distance, calories and time goals, not a climb target. There is no power off or standby step.

Toothbrush events (Philips Sonicare and Oral-B): the brush sends an `activity` event when a brushing is saved, with `brushing` finished (match `complete` true or false for a whole routine, `person` by name, `mode` and `durationS`), a `maintenance` event whose `brushHead` is warn or due when the brush head wears out, and a `fault` event with `brushFault` (error bits in hexadecimal). Its `brush_activity` (asleep, standby, brushing, paused, charging, off), `brush_mode`, `battery` and the head figure (`brush_head_wear` on a Sonicare, `brush_head_days_left` on an Oral-B; use a crossing) are `device` state signals and conditions. Activity and pickup changes are seen only while the brush's adverts reach a phone, so they can be late. A `device.set` can change the mode (on a Sonicare also intensity and the feedback switches) only on a handle that writes, with the owner's consent, while it is awake and not brushing; it never starts a brush.

Printer events: the printer plugin is the signal source `plugin_printer`. Its kinds are `job_started` and `job_finished` (match `result` such as completed, canceled or aborted, plus `person` and `pages`), `problem_added` and `problem_cleared` (match `keyword` such as media-jam-error, `severity` and `part`), `alert`, `supply_low`, `supply_empty` and `supply_replaced` (match `supply` and `key`; the level is in the data), `restarted`, `config_changed`, `pairing_problem` (match `reason`) and `offline_long` (30 minutes without an answer). Every event carries `printer` (name) and `printer_id`; match `printer` to pick one. Low and empty events follow the owner's notification switches and the printer's low threshold. Its state, queue, pages today, supplies and trays are `device` state signals.

Speech triggers (`trigger.speech`) match literal words or a contiguous phrase of finalized speech. `signal_read` view speech_sources shows the cameras, plugins and chats that can be chosen; leave `source` out for every authorized source. Bot speech is ignored unless `includeBots` is set; only the person who saved a speech automation may change it.

## Triggers and timing

Triggers are entry nodes: `trigger.device` (one device or a whole room, group or family), `trigger.signal`, `trigger.time`, `trigger.interval`, `trigger.sun`, `trigger.speech`, `trigger.presence`, `trigger.camera`, `trigger.button`, `trigger.called`, `trigger.value`, the run-status trigger, the device-health trigger and the later ones listed below; the catalog lists each one's outputs, and a node reads them with a wire from `trigger` and the output name, together with the ports `key` (which trigger fired) and `at`. A device or signal trigger takes a `test` (`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `between`, `in`, `changed`), a `window` (average, min, max, count or rate over a time) and these timing ports, all durations unless noted:

- `hold`: the test must stay true that long. `debounce`: decide only after no new signal for that long. `cooldown`: fire at most once in that long.
- `silentFor` (1 second to 7 days) fires when no matching signal arrived for that long, for example no motion in the hallway for 2 hours; it starts counting when the automation is enabled, every matching signal restarts it, it survives a hub restart, fires once per silence, and takes only `cooldown` besides it.
- `first` (`day`, `week` or `ever`) lets only the first match in the home day, the home week (Monday start) or ever fire, remembered across restarts; a match held back by `cooldown` does not use it up.
- `rearm` is a number for hysteresis on a `gt`, `gte`, `lt` or `lte` test: after firing on `gt` 28 with `rearm` 26 it fires again only after the value went below 26 (for `lt` and `lte` above it); `rearm` lies on the far side of the test value.
- `ignoreOwnChanges` (on by default) keeps an automation from triggering on its own commands; leave it on unless the person wants the loop.

The later triggers:

- `trigger.becomes_true` takes a `condition` (a wire to a flag from the read and calculation steps at the very start of the program) and an optional `hold`. It is checked only when something the condition reads changes, never on a timer, and fires on the change from false to true: not when the condition is already true as the automation is saved or the hub starts, and with `hold` only after it stayed true that long. A condition that fails, for example on a missing value, counts as false and the reason is logged.
- `trigger.computer` (`computer`, `kind` `app_open`, `app_focus`, `app_close`, `app_unfocus`, `power` or `power_<action>` such as `power_lock_screen`, plus `app` and `title`), `trigger.phone` (`phone`, `kind` `unlocked`, `context_changed`, `parked`, `charger_plugged`, `charger_unplugged`, `call_started`, `call_ended` or `notification_count_changed`, plus `to` and `from` for a change of activity, picked from the contexts the phone reports), `trigger.health` (`kind` `sleep_ended`, `body_reading`, `today` or `logged`, plus `person`, `metric` and the timing ports) and `trigger.chat` (`chat`, `outcome` `answered` or `failed`) start on what the hub already sees.
- `trigger.appliance` (`device` or `room`, or neither for every appliance; `event` `cycle_finished`, `maintenance` or `fault`; outputs `device`, `kind` and `detail`, the program, part or fault code), `trigger.safety` (`device`, `room` or neither; `kind` `leak`, `smoke`, `gas` or `alarm`; outputs `device`, `kind`) and `trigger.vacuum` (`vacuum`, or empty for every robot; `event` `started`, `finished`, `error`, `docked`, `needs_emptying` or `consumable_low`; outputs `vacuum`, `event`, `rooms` as the robot map names them, `fault`) are first-class: use them, not `trigger.signal` or `trigger.device` with free text.
- `trigger.weather` starts the moment new weather arrives and something changed (no change, no start; the feed refreshes every 15 minutes). `event` is `changed` (a `metric` such as temperature, feels_like, humidity, precipitation, wind_speed, uv_index or aqi, with a `test` and, to fire once per crossing, `rearm` a little past it on the other side, for example test above 25 and rearm 24), `band` (a `metric` moving into another band, `to` and `from`: temperature and feels_like freezing, cold, cool, mild, warm or hot; humidity dry, comfortable or humid; precipitation none, light, moderate or heavy; cloud_cover clear, partly_cloudy or overcast; wind_speed calm, breezy, windy, gale or storm; uv_index low, moderate, high, very_high or extreme; aqi good, fair, moderate, poor, bad or severe), `condition` (`to` and `from` clear, partly_cloudy, cloudy, fog, drizzle, rain, snow or storm), `rain_started` (optional `falling`), `rain_stopped`, `rain_expected` (`within` 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 3h or 6h, from the hourly forecast) or `forecast` (every update). For rain use `rain_started` and `rain_stopped`, never a polling interval with a weather read.
- `trigger.event` starts on the `signal.emit` step that sends the same `name`; `trigger.timer` starts when the Timer step of that `name` ends, also when the hub was down at the time; `trigger.hub_started` starts once each time the hub starts; `trigger.schedule` starts at each block of a weekly plan.
- `trigger.webhook` is for owners. Its `path` is the secret: 16 to 128 letters, digits, dashes or underscores, and the address is `/hooks/<path>` on the hub (GET, POST, PUT or DELETE, or the one `method` chosen). The run reads `trigger.method`, `trigger.body`, `trigger.headers` and `trigger.query`. An `http.respond` step answers the caller; without one the caller gets 202 as soon as the run waits, or 204 when it ends, and 500 with the reason when it fails.

## Plugin triggers

A plugin declares its own triggers, and each event it declares becomes a trigger unless the plugin turned that off. They are in the catalog group `plugins` with `origin` and `available` (an unavailable one carries the reason: plugin off, external local process, owner only; tell the person instead of rebuilding it with `trigger.signal`), and their ids are `trigger.plugin.<owner>.<id>`, the owner being the plugin id with `-` as `_`, or `driver_<id>` for a local driver. Their filters are pickers over the plugin's entities: read choices with `plugin_read`.

Use for “when the door opens at night turn on the hall light”, “remind me in 20 minutes”, “make a movie scene” or “why didn’t my automation run”.
